ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: the covered stretch shows one unexempted off-route segment (F4) on a metered RydeTAXI trip, but the GPS trace ends 4 min before drop-off (F1) and the billed 12.17 km (F7) exceeds the 10.2 km GPS total (F2), so the RD-2 refund cannot be computed from the record; ask the reviewer to obtain the full trace/fare record and decide whether to levy the segment-based refund without any account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider complains the driver took a different way on a metered RydeTAXI trip (estimate 7.2 km, meter 12 km) and wants the extra distance back [F2][F7][RD-1]. The covered trace shows one off-route segment 09:04–09:14 driving 5.23 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, +4.15 km and up to 1989 m off route [F4], which on its face is an unexplained breach of the shortest-and-most-direct duty [F4][RD-1].

Nothing exempts that segment. The complete, fully timestamped chat [F10] contains only the rider's 08:47 pickup note about waiting outside Beach Station with a black backpack [F8] and the driver's 08:48 "on my way" note [F9]; no rider message before 09:04 agrees to any route change [F8][F9][RD-5], and a driver's post-trip claim is not consent [F11][RD-5]. The traffic record gives no reasonable cause: no incident near the route in the window [F14], and only speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Eu Tong Sen Street and Sentosa Gateway [F12][F13], which is not band 1/2 and is at most corroborative anyway [RD-4]. Fair weather removes any weather excuse [F15][RD-4]. So the segment counts as unexempted [F4][RD-2].

The refund therefore belongs on the meter: RydeTAXI bills by distance unit, so extra kilometres enter the fare directly [F7][RD-2]. But the amount cannot be fixed on this record. The trace does not cover the whole trip — the last sample is 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off [F1] — and the fare record bills 12.17 km ($17.16 ÷ $1.4100/km) [F7] while the GPS total is 10.2 km [F2], an unattributed 1.97 km gap, in addition to the 4.99 km excess-billing fact [F5] which RD-2 refuses to refund where the mileage is not attributed to a segment [F5][F2][F7][RD-2]. The covered-segment figure (4.15 km × $1.4100/km ≈ $5.85) rests only on F4 while the uncovered stretch is unmeasured [F1], so neither $7.04 [F5] nor $5.85 is settled by the record [F1][F4][RD-2]. Per the no-gap rule, missing evidence is not read in either side's favour, so the case goes to a person.

The RD-6 add-on is not triggered: the driver profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 d, none route-related [F17], so even a finding against him would not make this "repeated" enough to send his account to review, and profile facts cannot decide the deviation itself [F17][RD-6]. The rider's own clean profile is likewise only context [F16][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages [F8][F9], the driver's statement [F11] and the complaint; they contain only a pickup note, an ETA note, a route-justification claim and a fare grievance — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].
ruling.escalation_reason: evidence insufficient: The GPS trace does not cover the whole trip: the last sample is 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off [F1], and the fare record bills 12.17 km [F7] against a 10.2 km GPS total [F2] (1.97 km unattributed). Without the full trace/fare record the off-route segment's extra kilometres and hence the RD-2 refund cannot be computed from the record.

segment_findings.reason: The only messages before the 09:04 segment are the rider's 08:47 pickup note and the driver's 08:48 'on my way' note, so no rider message agrees to a route change; the driver's post-trip 'the GPS rerouted' statement is a claim, not consent [F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-5]. No incident was recorded and the corridor shows only band 3, not severe congestion [F14][F12][F13][RD-4], so the segment is unexempted and its extra km are refundable in principle [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The $7.04 refund is computed from the 4.99 km excess-billing fact [F5], and RD-2 refuses mileage not attributed to any off-route segment; the trace ends 4 min before drop-off [F1] and the billed 12.17 km [F7] exceeds the 10.2 km GPS total [F2], leaving 1.97 km unattributed, so the amount is not computable from this record [F1][F5][F7][F2][RD-2].
RD-6 requires an upheld route dispute in the last 90 days; the driver profile shows 1 upheld dispute but none route-related [F17], and profile facts cannot establish the deviation itself [F17][RD-6].

This claim (the driver's 'GPS rerouted' statement is not consent or reasonable cause) is correct and adopted in the segment finding; it does not, however, cure the evidentiary gap that blocks an executable amount [F11][F10][F14][F1][RD-5][RD-4].

The uncovered tail [F1] does prevent measuring the whole trip, but the covered segment F4 is fully measured and unexempted [F4][RD-1]; the gap matters not to liability on the segment but to computing the RD-2 amount, which is why the case escalates [F1][F2][F7][RD-2].

Confining the refund to segment extra kilometres is correct as a matter of RD-2 [F4][F5][RD-2], but the resulting figure ($5.85) cannot be verified against the billed 12.17 km / GPS 10.2 km mismatch with the trace ending 4 min early [F7][F2][F1], so no_action is not available and the amount is left to a human.
